File it with the fee (check) at Code Enforcement, Town Hall, 225 Main Street, 2nd floor.

resale_co.notes: The Township code (ecode360, seen only as search result text) requires a Township certificate of compliance before anyone uses or occupies a building, and the Code Enforcement Certificate of Compliance form has a Resale option with fees of $100.00 for a single or two family home. The same form covers rentals ($100.00 for an individual rental unit within a multiple dwelling). Search summaries also mention a temporary certificate for up to 30 days and fees set in Chapter 71, but the Chapter 71 amounts could not be seen in exact words, so only the form amounts are used. The form does not state the payment method beyond a check number line, or how long the certificate is valid. The Building Department page shows Township emails as @LITTLEFALLSNJ.GOV, while the underlying page links point to older @lfnj.com addresses; the displayed addresses are used here. Lead paint inspections for rentals are a separate Township application.

requirements: Smoke alarms on each level including the basement and outside each separate sleeping area; a photoelectric smoke alarm if a bedroom is within 10 feet of the kitchen
Smoke alarms permanently mounted on the ceiling or within 12 inches of the ceiling on the wall
Battery-only smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed battery units (UL 217); hardwired alarms may not be replaced with battery alarms
Smoke alarms in service more than 10 years must be replaced
Central station fire alarm systems must be tested before the inspection and a test report submitted, or the inspection fails
CO alarm within 10 feet of each sleeping area when the home has a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage (battery, hardwired or plug-in)
Secondary power source label (for example CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER, not handwritten) within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter
Fire extinguishers are no longer required to pass inspection and are optional

authorities.how_to_apply: Get the One and Two Family Dwelling application packet from the Fire Prevention Bureau (Town Hall, 2nd floor) or the Township website. Complete it in full, signed by both seller and buyer, and return it in person to the Fire Prevention Bureau with the fee; check or money order payable to Township of Little Falls only. The inspection date is set then; someone 18 or older must be present.

fire_cert.notes: The Little Falls Fire Department (Bureau of Fire Prevention) is the fire code enforcing agency and issues the resale smoke and carbon monoxide alarm certificate; this is separate from the Township Code Enforcement Certificate of Compliance and has its own fee. The packet's cover form is titled for smoke detector, carbon monoxide and fire extinguisher certification, but its instructions say extinguishers are no longer required and are optional. The packet says an owner who sells or rents without the inspection will be fined. The Fire Prevention page displays Township emails as @LITTLEFALLSNJ.GOV while its links point to @lfnj.com; the state directory still lists JDiMaria@lfnj.com.
